transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
Honestly, I'm here because I've been struggling with constant, overwhelming worry and anxiety. It feels like it's there almost every day, and I just can't seem to control or stop it.
I'm sorry to hear you've been dealing with that. How long have you been experiencing this constant worry and anxiety?
I've been dealing with this constant worry for about a year and seven months now. It's just so exhausting because it feels like there hasn't been a single day of relief in all that time.
What kinds of things do you find yourself worrying about the most? Are they usually everyday concerns like family, work, and health?

Yes, that's exactly it. My worries aren't focused on just one thing; they seem to spread to almost every area of my life, like my family, my work, and our finances. It feels like I'm constantly stressing over all these everyday things all at once.
Along with this worry, have you been experiencing physical symptoms like muscle tension, trouble sleeping, restlessness, or feeling constantly fatigued?

To be honest, I haven't really noticed those kinds of physical symptoms like muscle tension or trouble sleeping. My main struggle is just the constant, uncontrollable mental worry that I can't seem to turn off.
Alongside this worry, have you been experiencing a persistently down or depressed mood, or have you lost interest or pleasure in the things you normally enjoy?
No, I don't really feel persistently down or depressed, and I haven't lost interest in my usual activities. My main struggle is just this constant, overwhelming worry that I can't seem to turn off.
Do you experience repetitive, unwanted thoughts or images that pop into your mind and cause distress, or do you feel driven to perform certain behaviors or mental routines to ease your anxiety?

No, I don't experience those kinds of unwanted images, and I don't have any special routines or rituals that I feel driven to do to ease my anxiety. I definitely get general worries that suddenly pop into my head and distract me, but I don't do anything specific to try and stop them.
Have you ever experienced or witnessed a highly traumatic or life-threatening event, and do you find yourself having nightmares or flashbacks related to it?
No, I have never experienced or witnessed any highly traumatic or life-threatening events. I also don't have any nightmares or flashbacks.
Do you find that this constant worry makes it difficult for you to concentrate on your daily tasks, or have you been feeling more irritable than usual?

Yes, absolutely. The worries constantly pop into my head, making it incredibly difficult to concentrate or focus on my daily tasks. I haven't really noticed feeling more irritable, but the lack of focus from these intrusive thoughts is a major struggle for me.
Do you often feel restless, keyed up, or on edge, or do you find yourself getting tired or fatigued very easily?

I haven't really noticed feeling physically restless, keyed up, or easily fatigued. My struggle is much more mental, with the constant worrying and the complete inability to control my thoughts once they start.
Did you struggle with concentration, organization, or forgetfulness during your childhood, or did these focus issues only start when your worries began?
I don't remember having any focus or organization problems during my childhood. These concentration issues really only started once my worries became so constant and overwhelming.
